newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 6.0/7.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 6.0/7.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money fell to 6.0/7.0 percent from 8.0/10.0 percent on Thursday morning on the back of ample rupiah supply, dealers said.
They said liquidity injection following central bank dollar buying on Tuesday caused some oversupply in the market.
The central bank was estimated to have bought some $400 million from the market to keep the dollar trading within the intervention band.
But operators were concerned over Friday liquidity.
Dealers said there have been sharp swings in money market trading on previous Fridays, with overnight money sometimes sky-rocketing to a high of some 30 percent due to tight conditions.
"Operators seem to expect a relatively tight money market tomorrow, as reflected by rising tom/next swaps," one said.
Overnight swap fell to 0.1/0.3 points from 0.3/0.4, but tom/next swap rose to 2.00/2.25 from 1.6/1.7 points.
One foreign bank dealer said longer-term money was little changed, with one-week money quoted at 13.75 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Wednesday was 9.51 percent, compared with 13.80 percent on Tuesday.
